name: United Kingdom
known: Financial services and London as a global city
Old universities, football and the Premier League
Music, theatre, film and television exports
Pharmaceuticals, aerospace and design
facts: It is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, each with its own traditions and some separate laws.
The National Health Service has provided mostly free healthcare since 1948.
The UK left the European Union on 31 January 2020.
Traffic drives on the left, as in Singapore.

name: Ireland
known: European bases of big technology and pharmaceutical companies
Writers such as Joyce, Yeats and Heaney
Guinness, music and pub culture
Green countryside and the Cliffs of Moher
facts: The Republic of Ireland became independent from the UK in stages, as the Irish Free State in 1922 and a republic in 1949.
It uses the euro and belongs to the European Union, while Northern Ireland stays in the UK.
English is spoken everywhere; Irish is the first official language and is taught in all schools.
Dublin is the capital and by far the largest city.

name: Germany
known: Cars and precision engineering
A strong base of mid-sized specialist manufacturers
Apprenticeship-based vocational training
Beer, bread, Christmas markets and castles
facts: It has the largest economy in the European Union.
East and West Germany were reunited on 3 October 1990.
It is a federation of 16 states, each with its own government and responsibility for education.
Public universities charge little or no tuition fees, including to many international students.

name: France
known: Fashion, luxury goods, perfume and cosmetics
Food, wine and cheese
Paris, the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre
Aerospace, trains and nuclear power
facts: It is one of the most visited countries in the world.
The Fifth Republic, with a strong president, has run the country since 1958.
Overseas regions such as Guadeloupe, Martinique and Réunion are part of France and of the European Union.
Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics.

name: Netherlands
known: Cycling, canals and tulips
Water management and flood defences
Trade, with Rotterdam as Europe's largest port
Advanced chipmaking equipment and food exports
facts: About a quarter of the country lies below sea level, protected by dikes, dunes and pumps.
Amsterdam is the capital, but the government sits in The Hague.
Many degree programmes at research universities are taught in English, and Dutch people widely speak English.
The Kingdom of the Netherlands also includes Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten in the Caribbean.

name: Switzerland
known: Banking, private wealth and insurance
Watches, chocolate and cheese
Pharmaceuticals and medical technology
The Alps, skiing and an extremely punctual rail network
facts: It has four national languages, and different regions (cantons) use different ones.
Switzerland is not in the European Union but has close agreements with it, and it keeps its own currency, the Swiss franc.
Voters decide many national questions in referendums several times a year.
It has a long-standing policy of neutrality and has not taken part in a foreign war since 1815.

name: Sweden
known: Design and flat-pack furniture
Start-ups and music exports
The Nobel Prizes, presented in Stockholm
Engineering, from trucks and cars to telecoms equipment
facts: Sweden is in the European Union but kept its own currency, the Swedish krona.
It joined NATO in 2024, ending more than 200 years of military non-alignment.
A right of public access lets anyone walk, camp and pick berries on most land.
Most of the country's people live in the southern third.

name: Norway
known: Oil and gas from the North Sea
Fjords, mountains and the northern lights
Hydropower, shipping and salmon farming
The highest share of electric cars in the world
facts: Norway is not in the European Union but takes part in its single market through the European Economic Area.
Its government pension fund, built from oil income, is one of the largest investment funds in the world.
Above the Arctic Circle the sun does not set for weeks in summer and does not rise for weeks in winter.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, while the other Nobel prizes are awarded in Stockholm.

unis.n: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

name: Denmark
known: Wind energy and green technology
Design, Lego and architecture
Medicines for diabetes and obesity
Container shipping and cycling cities
facts: Denmark is in the European Union but kept its own currency, the Danish krone.
The Faroe Islands and Greenland are self-governing parts of the Danish realm.
Most workers can be hired and let go easily, while the state supports them in between jobs and with retraining.
Copenhagen is the capital and largest city.

name: Finland
known: A school system often held up as a model
Telecoms and electronics, from Nokia to start-ups
Video games such as Angry Birds
Forests, lakes, saunas and Lapland
facts: Finnish and Swedish are both official languages, and Swedish is spoken by a small minority.
Finland joined NATO in 2023 and uses the euro.
Saunas are part of everyday life, in homes, apartment blocks and workplaces.
Finland shares a border of about 1,300 kilometres with Russia.

name: Italy
known: Fashion, design and luxury goods
Food and coffee, from pizza and pasta to espresso
Rome, Florence and Venice, with some of the world's most visited art and history
Sports cars, machinery and industrial design
facts: Italy has one of the largest numbers of UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country.
It became a single country in 1861; before that it was a patchwork of kingdoms and city states.
Vatican City, the seat of the Catholic Church, and San Marino are independent states inside Italian territory.
Italy uses the euro and is a founding member of what is now the European Union.

name: Spain
known: Tourism, beaches and sunshine
Football, with clubs such as Real Madrid and Barcelona
Food and drink, from paella and jamón to olive oil and wine
Fast fashion and renewable energy
facts: Catalan, Galician and Basque are co-official with Spanish in their own regions.
Spain became a democracy again after the death of the dictator Franco in 1975, and is now a constitutional monarchy.
It includes the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands and two small cities on the North African coast, Ceuta and Melilla.
Spanish is the official language of about 20 countries, so Spanish-taught study opens links with Latin America.

name: Russia
known: Being the largest country in the world by area
Oil, gas, metals and grain exports
Ballet, classical music and writers such as Tolstoy and Dostoevsky
Space firsts from the Soviet era, such as Sputnik and Yuri Gagarin
facts: It spans 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad in the west to Kamchatka in the east.
The Trans-Siberian Railway links Moscow to Vladivostok, about 9,300 kilometres away.
After Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, many countries imposed sanctions that restrict trade, banking and travel links with Russia.
Moscow is the capital; Saint Petersburg is the second-largest city.

name: Poland
known: Manufacturing, from furniture to buses and car parts
Software development and shared-services centres
Composer Chopin and scientist Marie Curie
Pierogi, amber and historic city centres such as Kraków
facts: Poland joined the European Union in 2004 but still uses its own currency, the złoty.
Warsaw's old town was almost completely destroyed in the Second World War and rebuilt, and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Marie Curie, who won Nobel Prizes in physics and chemistry, was born in Warsaw.
Its economy has grown strongly since the end of communism in 1989.

name: Belgium
known: Chocolate, beer, waffles and fries
Brussels as the home of major European Union institutions and NATO
Diamonds trading in Antwerp and a major port
Pharmaceuticals and chemicals
facts: Belgium has three official languages, and its regions and language communities each have their own governments.
The country became independent in 1830.
Brussels is the capital and hosts the European Commission and the headquarters of NATO.
Belgium uses the euro and is a founding member of what is now the European Union.

name: Austria
known: Classical music, from Mozart to the Vienna Philharmonic
Alpine skiing and mountain tourism
Coffee houses, cakes and imperial palaces in Vienna
Steel, machinery and energy drinks
facts: Vienna hosts offices of the United Nations and of OPEC.
Austria declared permanent neutrality in 1955 and joined the European Union in 1995.
It uses the euro and is landlocked.
Vienna was the capital of the Habsburg empire for centuries.
